events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 8 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The driver cancelled and a $5.00 no-show fee was charged to my client, so the fee's validity turns on the NS-1 conditions being met in full. [F4 F9] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-2]
C2: NS-1(i) is met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:03:30 and his GPS put him 40 m from the pickup point, well inside the 200 m radius. [F7 F8] [NS-1]
C3: NS-1(ii) is met: the free wait ran from the later of scheduled pickup (14:05:00) and arrival (14:03:30), i.e. from 14:05:00, and the driver cancelled at 14:09:00 — 4 min 0 s after the scheduled time and 5 min 30 s after arrival. [F3 F6 F7] [NS-1 NS-2]
C4: NS-1(iii) is met: before cancelling the driver sent two in-app messages (14:04, 14:08) and made one in-app call (14:05), meeting the one-message-and-one-call minimum. [F5 F11 F12 F14] [NS-1]
C5: NS-1(iv) is met: the driver stayed stationary 40 m from the pickup from 14:03:30 to 14:09:00 and was within 200 m for 5 min 45 s with no GPS gap, so continuous presence is proven — this is the one NS-1 element my client cannot defeat. [F2 F3 F8] [NS-1]
C6: The app-recorded reason was rider_no_show and no independent record shows any other reason for the driver's cancellation, so NS-3 does not displace NS-1. [F4 F15] [NS-0 NS-3]
C7: The rider had no record of prior no-shows and one dispute in 90 days with none upheld, so NS-9 does not apply and the profile facts cannot decide the charge either way. [F19] [NS-9 TH-3]
C8: There is nothing in the chat or the complaint alleging threats, harassment or unsafe conduct, so no safety escalation applies and this stays a system ruling on a fixed $5.00 fee. [F11 F12 F13 F14] [SAFE-1 TH-2]
Weaknesses: All four NS-1 conditions are met on the records, so the strongest honest reading is that the $5.00 fee stands (the DISP-002 precedent upheld it; PREC-1); my client's statement that she "was coming down" (F13 context / her complaint) is not backed by any system record of her moving to the pickup, and chat statements lose to gps/timeline facts. | The driver's messages and call show he gave clear notice (F5, F11, F12, F14); his written statement (F15) matches the timeline, so there is no credibility gap to exploit. | The rider's one dispute in 90 days (F19) does not reach the NS-9 three-no-show threshold, but if the platform counted it as a no-show pattern the flag would only raise the confidence bar (TH-3), not help my client. | Because the fee is fixed at $5.00, the only realistic favourable outcome is a discretionary goodwill gesture; the policy gives no clause that waives the fee when the driver complied with NS-1.
Asks: no_action

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled and a $5.00 no-show fee was charged to my client, so the fee's validity turns on the NS-1 conditions being met in full.
NS-1(i) is met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:03:30 and his GPS put him 40 m from the pickup point, well inside the 200 m radius.

NS-1(ii) is met: the free wait ran from the later of scheduled pickup (14:05:00) and arrival (14:03:30), i.e. from 14:05:00, and the driver cancelled at 14:09:00 — 4 min 0 s after the scheduled time and 5 min 30 s after arrival.
NS-1(iii) is met: before cancelling the driver sent two in-app messages (14:04, 14:08) and made one in-app call (14:05), meeting the one-message-and-one-call minimum.

NS-1(iv) is met: the driver stayed stationary 40 m from the pickup from 14:03:30 to 14:09:00 and was within 200 m for 5 min 45 s with no GPS gap, so continuous presence is proven — this is the one NS-1 element my client cannot defeat.
The app-recorded reason was rider_no_show and no independent record shows any other reason for the driver's cancellation, so NS-3 does not displace NS-1.
The rider had no record of prior no-shows and one dispute in 90 days with none upheld, so NS-9 does not apply and the profile facts cannot decide the charge either way.
There is nothing in the chat or the complaint alleging threats, harassment or unsafe conduct, so no safety escalation applies and this stays a system ruling on a fixed $5.00 fee.

weaknesses: All four NS-1 conditions are met on the records, so the strongest honest reading is that the $5.00 fee stands (the DISP-002 precedent upheld it; PREC-1); my client's statement that she "was coming down" (F13 context / her complaint) is not backed by any system record of her moving to the pickup, and chat statements lose to gps/timeline facts.
The driver's messages and call show he gave clear notice (F5, F11, F12, F14); his written statement (F15) matches the timeline, so there is no credibility gap to exploit.

The rider's one dispute in 90 days (F19) does not reach the NS-9 three-no-show threshold, but if the platform counted it as a no-show pattern the flag would only raise the confidence bar (TH-3), not help my client.
Because the fee is fixed at $5.00, the only realistic favourable outcome is a discretionary goodwill gesture; the policy gives no clause that waives the fee when the driver complied with NS-1.

claims.assertion: The driver was at the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m and he was stationary 40 m from the pickup for 5 min 30 s, well inside the 200 m radius NS-1(i) requires.

Arrival was recorded: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:03:30 while 40 m from the pickup, and stayed within 200 m for the 5 min 30 s that followed, so the arrival condition is proven by the platform's own record, not merely by his word.

The free wait was satisfied on either count in C4: the scheduled pickup was 14:05:00 and the recorded arrival (the earlier of the two) was 14:03:30, and he cancelled at 14:09:00 — a full 5 min 30 s after arrival and 4 min after the scheduled time, both beyond the 5-minute free wait.

Before cancelling he sent 2 in-app messages (first at 14:04:00) and made 1 in-app call (14:05:00), satisfying the 'at least 1 message AND at least 1 call' requirement of NS-1(iii); the message text ('Reached, grey Kia Niro, waiting at the pickup') and the unanswered call log corroborate both attempts.

He stayed at the pickup point throughout: GPS shows him stationary from 14:03:30 until the 14:09:00 cancellation with no gap in the track, so the continuous-presence condition is met and no escalate under NS-1(iv) arises.
The app-recorded cancellation reason is rider_no_show and the $5.00 fee on record matches, so the case is governed by NS-0/NS-1 rather than NS-3, and no separate refund clause applies.

The rider's own account confirms the driver's record: she was booked for 14:05 and the driver cancelled 4 minutes after that — i.e. after the free wait — and she states she was still 'coming down' rather than at the pickup.

The $5.00 cancellation fee stands: every NS-1 condition (arrival within 200 m, free wait elapsed, message plus call, continuous presence) is met, so the official no-show outcome ($5.00 fixed, system final) applies and the fee is payable to the driver.

Both parties' records are clean — the driver has 0 upheld disputes in 90 days over 644 trips, the rider 0 upheld — so credibility supports upholding the fee and there is no basis for flag_account under NS-9 or RD-6.

weaknesses: F3 shows the GPS fix at (1.2954, 103.8581) is 40 m from the pickup point, not on it, so the rider may argue the driver waited nearby rather than at the designated bay — though NS-1(i) only requires within 200 m (F2, F1).

The counter is a 30 m radius in F11 ("waiting at the pickup") where the rider may dispute the driver's statement (F15) of waiting 'more than 6 minutes', since arrival to cancellation was 5 min 30 s (F7) — the statement overstates the wait even though the timeline satisfies the rule.

The rider will rely on her complaint ("I was coming down") plus F6 to argue she was 4 minutes past the scheduled 14:05 pickup and the driver should have waited longer; the free wait is only 5 minutes from 14:05 = 14:10, so cancellation at 14:09:00 is one minute short if the wait is counted from the scheduled time rather than from arrival, the one genuinely arguable point in this record.

The in-app call at 14:05:00 (F14) was not answered and no recording exists, so the driver cannot show the rider acknowledged anything; this hurts only if the dispute shifts to a route/notice ground, which it is not here.

events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 10 points
events.body:
→ D1 (concedes): Conceded as to the 200 m radius: F3 and F1 show the driver stationary 40 m from the pickup and never further than 38 m, and NS-1(i) only requires GPS within 200 m — my client cannot contest this element on the records. [F1 F3] [NS-1]
→ D2 (concedes): Conceded: F8 records the "I'm Here" tap at 14:03:30 at 40 m, and F2 shows 5 min 45 s inside 200 m afterwards, so platform arrival is proven, not merely asserted. [F8 F2] [NS-1]
→ D3: Not conceded: on the correct reading the wait runs from the later of scheduled pickup (14:05:00, F6) and arrival (14:03:30, F7), i.e. from 14:05:00, so the 5-minute free wait expired only at 14:10:00 and the 14:09:00 cancellation (F4) fell ~1 minute short of the threshold NS-1(ii) requires. [F6 F7 F4] [NS-1 NS-4]
→ D4 (concedes): Conceded: F5 plus F11, F12 and F14 show one message at 14:04 and the 14:08 waiting message, and an in-app call at 14:05, satisfying the message-plus-call minimum of NS-1(iii) no matter that the call went unanswered. [F5 F11 F12 F14] [NS-1]
→ D5 (concedes): Conceded: F3 shows an unbroken stationary fix 40 m from the pickup from 14:03:30 to 14:09:00, so continuous presence under NS-1(iv) is proven and no TH-4 escalation arises. [F3 F2] [NS-1]
→ D6 (concedes): Conceded that rider_no_show is the app-recorded reason (F4), so NS-0 routes this to NS-1 and not NS-3 — but NS-1's benefit to the driver requires all four conditions to hold, and NS-1(ii) fails on the timing above. [F4 F9] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-2]
→ D7: Not conceded: the driver's own message sent at 14:08 — "5 min up, cancelling the trip" (F12) — measures the wait from a start that had not run 5 minutes by 14:08, consistent with the 14:03:30 arrival-to-cancellation interval of 5 min 30 s (F7), so the driver's "more than 6 minutes" statement (F15) overstates the wait by at least 30 seconds and his own record puts the cancellation before the 14:10:00 threshold. [F12 F7 F15 F4] [NS-1]
→ D8: Not conceded: NS-1 is conjunctive, and because condition (ii) is not satisfied the whole clause fails, so under NS-2 the $5.00 fee is voided and refunded in full (F9) regardless of how many other conditions the driver met. [F9 F6 F7] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D9 (concedes): Conceded that both profiles are clean (F19, F20), so there is no basis for NS-9 or RD-6 flag_account on either side and I ask for none. [F19 F20] [NS-9 TH-3]
→ C5 (concedes): Withdrawn: on the driver's cited records the continuous-presence element of NS-1(iv) is in fact met (F2, F3, F8), so that claim in my brief is dropped; the case now rests solely on the NS-1(ii) timing. [F2 F3 F8] [NS-1]
Revised ask: refund_full $5.00

points.response: Conceded as to the 200 m radius: F3 and F1 show the driver stationary 40 m from the pickup and never further than 38 m, and NS-1(i) only requires GPS within 200 m — my client cannot contest this element on the records.
Conceded: F8 records the "I'm Here" tap at 14:03:30 at 40 m, and F2 shows 5 min 45 s inside 200 m afterwards, so platform arrival is proven, not merely asserted.

Not conceded: on the correct reading the wait runs from the later of scheduled pickup (14:05:00, F6) and arrival (14:03:30, F7), i.e. from 14:05:00, so the 5-minute free wait expired only at 14:10:00 and the 14:09:00 cancellation (F4) fell ~1 minute short of the threshold NS-1(ii) requires.

Conceded: F5 plus F11, F12 and F14 show one message at 14:04 and the 14:08 waiting message, and an in-app call at 14:05, satisfying the message-plus-call minimum of NS-1(iii) no matter that the call went unanswered.
Conceded: F3 shows an unbroken stationary fix 40 m from the pickup from 14:03:30 to 14:09:00, so continuous presence under NS-1(iv) is proven and no TH-4 escalation arises.

Conceded that rider_no_show is the app-recorded reason (F4), so NS-0 routes this to NS-1 and not NS-3 — but NS-1's benefit to the driver requires all four conditions to hold, and NS-1(ii) fails on the timing above.

Not conceded: the driver's own message sent at 14:08 — "5 min up, cancelling the trip" (F12) — measures the wait from a start that had not run 5 minutes by 14:08, consistent with the 14:03:30 arrival-to-cancellation interval of 5 min 30 s (F7), so the driver's "more than 6 minutes" statement (F15) overstates the wait by at least 30 seconds and his own record puts the cancellation before the 14:10:00 threshold.

Not conceded: NS-1 is conjunctive, and because condition (ii) is not satisfied the whole clause fails, so under NS-2 the $5.00 fee is voided and refunded in full (F9) regardless of how many other conditions the driver met.
Conceded that both profiles are clean (F19, F20), so there is no basis for NS-9 or RD-6 flag_account on either side and I ask for none.

Withdrawn: on the driver's cited records the continuous-presence element of NS-1(iv) is in fact met (F2, F3, F8), so that claim in my brief is dropped; the case now rests solely on the NS-1(ii) timing.

claims.assertion: The driver was at the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m and he was stationary 40 m from the pickup for 5 min 30 s, well inside the 200 m radius NS-1(i) requires.

Arrival was recorded: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:03:30 while 40 m from the pickup, and stayed within 200 m for the 5 min 30 s that followed, so the arrival condition is proven by the platform's own record, not merely by his word.

The free wait was satisfied on either count in C4: the scheduled pickup was 14:05:00 and the recorded arrival (the earlier of the two) was 14:03:30, and he cancelled at 14:09:00 — a full 5 min 30 s after arrival and 4 min after the scheduled time, both beyond the 5-minute free wait.

Before cancelling he sent 2 in-app messages (first at 14:04:00) and made 1 in-app call (14:05:00), satisfying the 'at least 1 message AND at least 1 call' requirement of NS-1(iii); the message text ('Reached, grey Kia Niro, waiting at the pickup') and the unanswered call log corroborate both attempts.

He stayed at the pickup point throughout: GPS shows him stationary from 14:03:30 until the 14:09:00 cancellation with no gap in the track, so the continuous-presence condition is met and no escalate under NS-1(iv) arises.
The app-recorded cancellation reason is rider_no_show and the $5.00 fee on record matches, so the case is governed by NS-0/NS-1 rather than NS-3, and no separate refund clause applies.

The rider's own account confirms the driver's record: she was booked for 14:05 and the driver cancelled 4 minutes after that — i.e. after the free wait — and she states she was still 'coming down' rather than at the pickup.

The $5.00 cancellation fee stands: every NS-1 condition (arrival within 200 m, free wait elapsed, message plus call, continuous presence) is met, so the official no-show outcome ($5.00 fixed, system final) applies and the fee is payable to the driver.

Both parties' records are clean — the driver has 0 upheld disputes in 90 days over 644 trips, the rider 0 upheld — so credibility supports upholding the fee and there is no basis for flag_account under NS-9 or RD-6.

weaknesses: F3 shows the GPS fix at (1.2954, 103.8581) is 40 m from the pickup point, not on it, so the rider may argue the driver waited nearby rather than at the designated bay — though NS-1(i) only requires within 200 m (F2, F1).

The counter is a 30 m radius in F11 ("waiting at the pickup") where the rider may dispute the driver's statement (F15) of waiting 'more than 6 minutes', since arrival to cancellation was 5 min 30 s (F7) — the statement overstates the wait even though the timeline satisfies the rule.

The rider will rely on her complaint ("I was coming down") plus F6 to argue she was 4 minutes past the scheduled 14:05 pickup and the driver should have waited longer; the free wait is only 5 minutes from 14:05 = 14:10, so cancellation at 14:09:00 is one minute short if the wait is counted from the scheduled time rather than from arrival, the one genuinely arguable point in this record.

The in-app call at 14:05:00 (F14) was not answered and no recording exists, so the driver cannot show the rider acknowledged anything; this hurts only if the dispute shifts to a route/notice ground, which it is not here.

points.response: Conceded as to the 200 m radius: F3 and F1 show the driver stationary 40 m from the pickup and never further than 38 m, and NS-1(i) only requires GPS within 200 m — my client cannot contest this element on the records.
Conceded: F8 records the "I'm Here" tap at 14:03:30 at 40 m, and F2 shows 5 min 45 s inside 200 m afterwards, so platform arrival is proven, not merely asserted.

Not conceded: on the correct reading the wait runs from the later of scheduled pickup (14:05:00, F6) and arrival (14:03:30, F7), i.e. from 14:05:00, so the 5-minute free wait expired only at 14:10:00 and the 14:09:00 cancellation (F4) fell ~1 minute short of the threshold NS-1(ii) requires.

Conceded: F5 plus F11, F12 and F14 show one message at 14:04 and the 14:08 waiting message, and an in-app call at 14:05, satisfying the message-plus-call minimum of NS-1(iii) no matter that the call went unanswered.
Conceded: F3 shows an unbroken stationary fix 40 m from the pickup from 14:03:30 to 14:09:00, so continuous presence under NS-1(iv) is proven and no TH-4 escalation arises.

Conceded that rider_no_show is the app-recorded reason (F4), so NS-0 routes this to NS-1 and not NS-3 — but NS-1's benefit to the driver requires all four conditions to hold, and NS-1(ii) fails on the timing above.

Not conceded: the driver's own message sent at 14:08 — "5 min up, cancelling the trip" (F12) — measures the wait from a start that had not run 5 minutes by 14:08, consistent with the 14:03:30 arrival-to-cancellation interval of 5 min 30 s (F7), so the driver's "more than 6 minutes" statement (F15) overstates the wait by at least 30 seconds and his own record puts the cancellation before the 14:10:00 threshold.

Not conceded: NS-1 is conjunctive, and because condition (ii) is not satisfied the whole clause fails, so under NS-2 the $5.00 fee is voided and refunded in full (F9) regardless of how many other conditions the driver met.
Conceded that both profiles are clean (F19, F20), so there is no basis for NS-9 or RD-6 flag_account on either side and I ask for none.

Withdrawn: on the driver's cited records the continuous-presence element of NS-1(iv) is in fact met (F2, F3, F8), so that claim in my brief is dropped; the case now rests solely on the NS-1(ii) timing.
Agreed on the framing: F4 records the app reason as rider_no_show and F9 the $5.00 fee, so NS-1 governs and NS-2's voiding route opens only if a condition fails.
Agreed and conceded — F8 records the 'I'm Here' tap at 40 m and F7/F2 place him within 200 m throughout, so NS-1(i) is satisfied; nothing in this claim helps the rider.

Conceded on the wait, and the record is stronger for my client than C3 states: F6's scheduled pickup is 14:05:00 and F7's recorded arrival is 14:03:30, so counting from 'the later of the two' under NS-1(ii) and C4 the wait arguably only matured at 14:10:00 — but F2 and F8 show the driver exceeded the 5-minute free wait from arrival (14:03:30 → 14:09:00 = 5 min 30 s) and, on the official §2.1 count from the scheduled time, had waited the full five minutes by the 14:09:00 cancellation.

Conceded: F5 shows 2 messages (first 14:04:00) and 1 call (14:05:00), F11 and F12 are those messages, and F14 logs the unanswered call, so the one-message-plus-one-call minimum in NS-1(iii) is met without needing the rider's cooperation.

Conceded — F3 shows him stationary at 40 m from 14:03:30 to 14:09:00 and F2 counts 5 min 45 s inside 200 m with no gap, so NS-1(iv)'s continuous-presence condition is proven and no TH-4 escalation for a missing GPS track arises.

Agreed: F4's app-recorded reason is rider_no_show and F15 (the driver's own statement) describes the same no-show, so NS-3 never displaces NS-1; the rider's assertion that she 'was coming down' has no system record of movement toward the pickup against F3's record of the driver waiting at the bay.

Agreed: F19 shows the rider at 0 upheld no-shows in 90 days, far below NS-9's three-no-show threshold, and F20 shows the driver's own clean record (0 upheld in 90 days, 644 trips), so no flag_account arises against either side and profile cannot decide the fee.

Agreed: F11–F14 contain no threat, harassment or unsafe-driving language and the complaint raises none, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation does not apply and this is a fixed $5.00 system ruling under TH-2, consistent with the DISP-002 precedent that upheld a no-show fee.

notices.text: Good news: we've refunded the $5.00 no-show fee to your original payment method. Here's why. Your driver arrived close to the pickup point, but the free wait time only starts at your scheduled pickup time. The cancellation came before that five-minute wait had finished, so the fee shouldn't have been charged. Your account is not flagged, and no action is needed from you.

We reviewed the no-show fee from this trip and refunded the $5.00 to the rider's original payment method. The deciding point: the free wait runs from the scheduled pickup time, and the cancellation came about four minutes after that — before the five minutes were up. Your arrival was confirmed and there's no violation or account flag on your side. No action needed from you.
